findings.rule: Policy in force at incident date and peril covered under product tier. Own damage collision under TPFT must be declined; uninsured motorist extension requires not-at-fault insured and an identified at-fault third party.
findings.explanation: Incident date 2026-08-17 is within the period of cover (2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31), premium was paid, and the incident was in Australia. v6.0 applies as the incident is after 2026-03-01. TPFT does not cover own damage from collision (clause 1.1), the peril is not fire or theft, and the uninsured motorist extension does not apply because the insured was at fault and no third party was identified (clause 1.3). The denial under POL-MTR-002:1.2 is consistent with cover rules.

findings.rule: A claim must be notified within 30 calendar days of the incident date (clause 2.1). Beyond 90 days it must be declined unless a 2.3 exception is approved.
findings.calculation: days_incident_to_fnol = 1, which is within the 30-day window (1 <= 30). No exception is needed.
findings.explanation: The claim was notified 1 day after the incident, inside the 30-day window in clause 2.1. Clauses 2.2 and 2.3 are not triggered, so no late-notification exception was required and none was applied.

findings.rule: No supplied exclusion applies: vehicle use matches declared use (3.7); no override recorded. Other exclusion types (alcohol, drugs, licence, unlisted driver, registration) have no supplied clauses and no facts that trigger them.
findings.explanation: The only supplied exclusion that could apply to the facts is commercial/hire use (3.7, absolute). Declared and actual use are both PRIVATE, so it is not triggered. The theft-related rebuttable exclusion (3.13) is not relevant to a collision. No override or exception was recorded, so none was invalid. The denial on the ground of TPFT not covering own-damage collision is a coverage matter, not an exclusion matter, and is outside this area.

findings.rule: Tracks are tested in order (SIU, Complex, Fast-track, Standard); the first track whose criteria are met is assigned. Triage must occur within 1 business day of lodgement.
findings.calculation: Order 1 SIU: score 0 < 60, no indicators, so no trigger. Order 2 Complex: value 40000 not > 50000, no injury, liability clear, no total loss, so not met. Order 3 Fast-track: value 40000 > 5000, so not met. Order 4 Standard: all other claims, so assigned. Triage took 1 business day, within the 1 business day limit.
findings.explanation: The claim does not meet SIU, Complex or Fast-track criteria, so Standard is the correct track. It was triaged within 1 business day of lodgement. No re-triage was needed because the value did not cross a track boundary.

findings.rule: The supplied clauses say an assessment is required for all claims except fast-track claims where photos establish quantum (4.1). This claim is on the STANDARD track, so an assessment was required, and a DESKTOP assessment was done. The clauses do not say whether a desktop assessment satisfies the requirement for a non-fast-track claim, or what timeframe applies to a desktop assessment. The 4.2 timeframes apply only to a field assessment, which has not been shown to be required. The clauses also do not say whether an assessment is needed on a claim denied on cover grounds.
findings.explanation: An assessment was done 3 business days after triage, but no supplied clause defines when a desktop assessment is acceptable or sets its timeframe. Clause 4.2 covers field assessments only. A reviewer needs to confirm the missing rule on assessment type and timing.

findings.rule: A second assessment is required only on a written dispute, a variance above the greater of 30% or AUD 20,000, or a recorded conflict of interest. The assessment must be under 90 days old at decision. Independent external assessment is required only above AUD 100,000.
findings.calculation: Variance = 40000 - 38500 = 1500, which is 3.75% of 40000. The threshold is the greater of 30% (12000) and 20000, so 20000. 1500 < 20000, so a second assessment is not triggered. The assessment is 2 days old at decision, which is under 90. The claimed value of 40000 is under 100000, so no independent external assessor is required.
findings.explanation: No second assessment trigger is met on the facts supplied. The assessment was not stale, and the value is under the independent assessor threshold.

findings.rule: A denial above the approver's denial limit (measured against claimed value) must be escalated; every denial with claimed value above AUD 25,000 must be peer-reviewed by a second officer at L3 or above before being communicated.
findings.calculation: L2 denial authority = 25,000. Claimed amount 40,000 > 25,000, so it exceeds L2 denial limit by 15,000. Within L3 limit (100,000), so L3 approval was required. Claimed 40,000 > 25,000 so peer review by L3+ required; second_approver_level is null, so none recorded.
findings.explanation: The denial was approved by an L2 officer whose denial authority is capped at AUD 25,000, but the claimed value is AUD 40,000, so it needed escalation (L3 or above). No catastrophe surge applies, and surge does not raise denial authority anyway. The denial also lacked the mandatory L3+ peer review before it was communicated on 2026-08-27. These are two distinct failures: outside denial authority and missing peer review. The denial is outside authority and must be re-approved.

findings.rule: Every denial with claimed value above AUD 25,000 must be peer-reviewed by a second officer at Level 3 or above before being communicated.
findings.calculation: 40,000 > 25,000 so peer review required; none recorded.
findings.explanation: The required second-officer peer review at L3 or above was not recorded before the denial was communicated, a required step skipped.

findings.rule: Fraud score must be correctly calculated from triggered indicators, and the action required by the score band and any mandatory referral triggers must be followed. A score of 0-29 is Low and proceeds with normal handling.
findings.calculation: No indicators triggered, so the sum of points is 0 and the score is 0 (cap of 100 not relevant). The recorded score of 0 matches. Band is Low (0-29), so no enhanced verification or SIU referral is required. Claimed amount 40000 is below the 250,000 threshold in 5.1(e), and no 5.1 trigger is recorded.
findings.explanation: No fraud indicators are recorded, the recorded score of 0 matches the calculated score, and the Low band requires only normal handling. No mandatory referral triggers apply, so the absence of an SIU referral and enhanced verification is compliant.

findings.rule: Decision-stage documents required for the claim must be on file before a deny decision; settlement-stage documents are not required where the claim is denied.
findings.explanation: Decision-stage codes required: CLAIM_FORM, ID_VERIFIED (all claims), DRIVER_LICENCE (motor, driver in control), PHOTOS (motor), LICENCE_VERIFIED (claimed 40,000 > 10,000). All are on file. STAT_DEC is not required as 40,000 is not above 50,000. No third party, injury or theft, so TP_DETAILS and CTP_REFERENCE do not apply. POLICE_EVENT applies only to theft, malicious damage or collisions under clause 4.1 (not supplied), and no exception was relied on. Settlement-stage documents (e.g. VEHICLE_HISTORY_CHECK, ASSESSMENT_REPORT, repair quotes) are not required because the claim was denied.

findings.rule: Acknowledgement within 2 business days of lodgement; decision within 20 business days of docs-complete (standard track) and within 4 months of lodgement; decision communicated within 5 business days; status updates at least every 20 business days; payment within 10 business days of acceptance (not applicable, no payment).
findings.explanation: Acknowledgement took 1 business day (limit 2). Decision came 2 business days after docs complete (limit 20 for a standard claim) and within the 4-month cap. Decision was communicated in 1 business day (limit 5). The longest contact gap was 3 business days (limit 20). No settlement was offered or accepted, so the payment timeframe does not apply.

findings.rule: Settlement, excess, ITC, total loss and recovery calculations apply only where a claim is paid. This claim was denied, so no settlement was made and every settlement amount is zero.
findings.explanation: The claim was denied, so there is no settlement to check. Gross settlement, excess, GST/ITC deduction and net paid are all 0, which is consistent with a denial. The repair cost is 137.5% of value, above the 75% total loss threshold in POL-STL-007:2.1. The total_loss flag is false and no total loss declaration was recorded. This does not affect the settlement because nothing was paid. Whether the denial itself was correct is a coverage question outside this area.
